messages.subject: [Bug] The Report Option "-R" Crashes featureCounts
parts:
[Bug] The Report Option "-R" Crashes featureCounts

Version: Subread 1.6.1

OS: Red Hat Enterprise Linux 7.5, macOS 10.13.4

Compiler: gcc (GCC) 7.3.1 20180130 (Red Hat 7.3.1-4) in RHEL, Apple LLVM version 9.1.0 (clang-902.0.39.1) in macOS

Steps:

  1. Run featureCounts on the supplied BAM file (generated by STAR 2.5.4b) using the command line: featureCounts -a RefSeq.hg38.gtf -F GTF -t exon -g gene_id -J -s 0 -T 1 -R SAM -o Read-Counts.txt Test.bam
  2. featureCounts program crashed with an error message:featureCounts: input-files.c:5381: SAM_pairer_run: Assertion `1 != corrected_run' failed., and a core dump file temp-core-128249-AC1F6B630334.sam.fixbam was generated.

Reproducibility

This bug can be reproduced everytime when above steps are followed.

Supplements

The data files used to reproduce the bug can be found at:
https://www.dropbox.com/sh/kfixqosghklvwo7/AAB4e5OEQhHJcySEo0B9ttjka?dl=0

Thanks for the very detailed report! I found that SAMtools cannot decode your BAM file: Please file the picture attached to this post: it reported an error message to STDOUT, and decoded no reads. If SAMtools cannot decode your BAM file, the behaviour of featureCounts is undefined.
 
The MD5 sum of the BAM file is cb1db8c49c825b2f85ab153836c695ec

(I was using SAMtools v1.1.)

Cheers,
Yang

Hi Yang,

Thank you for trying out different versions of Samtools exhaustively on the BAM file! Glad to see there are always some versions work!

One hint I noticed is that the Test.featureCounts.sam created by featureCounts before it crashes has one line less than the Test.sam (converted from Test.bam by Samtools). messages.author: bce99ba71cd48eea
messages.subject: Re: [Bug] The Report Option "-R" Crashes featureCounts
parts:
First, I found a bug in Samtools 1.2 (and presumably also in 1.0 and 1.1) in decoding type "B" extra tags (ie, the array-type tags). If the element type in the array is int8 or u_int8, and if the array tag is the last tag in the SAM line, Samtools will wrongly decide that the last element in the array breaks the memory boundary, thus it reports an error message and quits. I have built another BAM file that has the correct format, but Samtools 1.2 reported an error message on it. Your BAM file has a correct format.

I then found the bug in featureCounts that led to the error. The last block in your BAM file had only one read. FeatureCounts used a wrong variable to decide the block length, hence it tried to find the second read in the block. This made it running over the memory boundary. By fixing this bug, featueCounts worked properly on your BAM file. The next release should have this bug fixed; before that, you may sort your BAM file by using Samtools (no matter on coordinates or read names) before running featureCounts on it.

Hi Yang,

Thank you so much for the quick fix! This is awesome!

Yes my alignment results were generated by STAR 2.5.4b from a series of single-ended mRNA sequencing reads. Another BAM file Test2.bam that caused the crash was also uploaded to the Dropbox folder.

In terms of bugs, there are always regressions in software development, so it's hard to tell which versions have less bugs. When I looked at the download history of Samtools at SourceForge:

https://sourceforge.net/projects/samtools/files/samtools/

I saw that the current version 1.8 and the version used by Red Hat Enterprise Linux (EPEL repository) 0.1.19 rank top in the download statistics list. So it seems that end users can tell the difference between versions.

-Granville
